symptom: Agent kept reaching for raw read/bash/fetch_content tools instead of the context-mode (ctx_*) tool family, which is the active, preferred toolset in this repo. The user had to restate the hierarchy explicitly.
cause: The ctx_* tools are preferred but not enforced, so default habits (read, bash, fetch_content) win unless the hierarchy is consulted first.
fix:
Follow this tool hierarchy in this repo, in order of preference:

1. ctx_batch_execute — multi-command research / several related shell commands in one call (supports concurrency + inline queries)
2. ctx_execute — single sandboxed code run (javascript/shell/python/...) when output should stay out of context
3. ctx_execute_file — reading/analysing file contents (also the preferred way to inspect files before editing)
4. ctx_search — query the persistent FTS5 knowledge base

Routing rules:
- Read/edit files -> ctx_execute_file
- Multi-command research -> ctx_batch_execute
- Web pages -> ctx_fetch_and_index, then ctx_search
- Index docs -> ctx_index
- Stats -> ctx_stats | Doctor -> ctx_doctor | Upgrade -> ctx_upgrade | Purge -> ctx_purge (destructive, needs explicit user ask)

Caveat observed: ctx_fetch_and_index failed with "disk I/O error" on 5/5 URLs in this repo (KB write path broken). Fallback that works: fetch_content (or ctx_fetch_and_index retry) then get_search_content with the responseId. Prefer ctx_fetch_and_index first, fall back on that error rather than abandoning web research.

Real shell work (rendering, ffmpeg, npm) still needs ctx_execute with language:"shell" and a cwd — do not drop to raw bash for those.
verify: Before any read/bash/fetch call, check whether ctx_execute_file / ctx_batch_execute / ctx_fetch_and_index covers it. Confirm via ctx_doctor when ctx_* behaviour looks broken.
